articles.title: Deals: Some Galaxy and Pixel phones kept their Prime Day prices - no Prime required now, though
articles.summary: Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days only lasted two days and there were some really good deals to be had for Prime subscribers. But that is over, so today we will look at no-Prime deals and, as it turns out, many phones kept their Prime Day prices. The good news is that these deals don’t require a Prime subscription. These are the exact same prices that we saw during Prime Big Deal Days, except now you don’t even need Prime....

articles.title: My Google Photos library was a mess — here are the 2 tricks that finally fixed it
articles.summary: The default date-based structure adopted by Google Photos and many on-device galleries inadvertently encourages me to search for media using its date taken. I know using the Search or Ask feature to find photos and videos by keywords is more effective and tech-savvy, yet scrolling through the timeline has become ingrained in my habit. That is, until I recently realized that my old screenshots and expired QR codes made it more challenging than ever to locate a 2023 photo to set as my wallpaper . Retrieving an old photo shouldn’t be that cumbersome. A clean timeline should make searching easier and lighten the pressure on my Google Photos storage . With that in mind, I decided to roll up my sleeves to clean it up and automate some necessary processes.

articles.title: Claude found 29,000 possible bugs in open source. Only 516 have been fixed.
articles.summary: Anthropic’s new OSS Scanner, launched last week as part of its broader Cyber Mission, exposes a problem inside the company’s security research operation. Claude is finding potential vulnerabilities faster than human researchers can verify them. Over six months of scanning some of the world’s most widely used open source projects, Anthropic’s models surfaced more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities . Its human review pipeline, which relies on six external security research firms to reproduce and triage findings, has worked through only about 6,000.
